offscreen_narration.text:
Morgan could write a polished story from memory. That would be hard to check. We need a smaller packet: enough to show the boundary, the work, the hold, and the human decision, without dragging every underlying record into the room.

Chapter Twenty-One's Scoped Proof Loop has six fields: audience, scope, window, exclusions, export, and ledger. For the Harbor board reader, scope is one session-option paper case across one course planning window. Include the permitted job, evidence-status summary, handoff result, the staffing hold, Morgan's paper disposition, and the still-unapproved print request. Exclude raw source text, prompts, private reasoning, unrelated people, and any actual records. The packet records what is known and what is withheld. It does not certify agent quality or imply a session happened.

The workbook calls for capability boundaries, scoped trace references, approval decisions, cost authority summary, export metadata, and reviewer notes. Use course references and a course timestamp label, not a real log. Morgan reviews the proposed proof packet before any sharing. If a field cannot be safely summarized, mark it withheld with a reason. Redaction is a decision, not a blur laid over a screenshot. Here, the export is only a classroom outline; nothing is sent.

The same team then hears an idea: a tiny phone tool that helps volunteer coordinators compare workshop options. The temptation is to build it because it fits the Harbor story. Chapter Twenty-Two asks for a Foundry Test first: demand, monetization, builder fit, build velocity, differentiation, release readiness, and approval gates. The workbook proposes a weighted score out of one hundred. A score is useful only when each field has attributable evidence. Our class has no real market research, payer interview, or release review. Those fields stay unscored. A number without evidence would turn an idea into false proof.

Write the smallest safe next test: Morgan could ask for permission to research public demand and clarify who would pay. Even that is a proposed plan, not a provider call or outreach. No repository, tester invite, user data collection, price, store listing, or public claim follows from this lesson. A phone can display the packet and a hold status, but it cannot waive the gate. The valuable outcome may be a decision to shelve the idea. That saves time a rushed build would consume.

Pause. What would you leave out of the board packet even if it helped tell a better story?

Draft a Client-Safe Proof Packet outline for the Harbor planning case. State audience, scope, window, inclusions, exclusions, export review, and ledger fields. Redact the course trace in words rather than pasting it. Then make a Foundry Test for the volunteer-coordinator tool: mark each evidence field observed, missing, or unscored; name a payer question, a tiny proposed test, the human gate, and a stop condition. Use a fictional or approved example. Do not use private operational data, contact a person, create a repo, or generate a public claim.

Save revision twelve as a draft. Harbor now has a way to explain its held work and a way to examine a new idea without pretending either is ready to ship.

timing.rule: Retain exact speech in order; change picture only at a sentence-complete spoken handoff; one speaker at a time; preserve native presenter source frame rate and audio; re-time captions after native recordings.

visuals.use: Six-field scoped proof card with a visible inclusion column and exclusion column.
visuals.text_equivalent: approved plate needs final scene-specific text alternative before publication

cover.use: static poster and internal animatic only; video locked

operating_file.update_exact: `proof-and-foundry` → `proof` and `foundry-test`, revision 12, status `draft`; revision 11's staffing and spend holds remain visible.

continuity.source_ids_policy: protected synthetic trace only; no source IDs in provider request

gates: purpose-specific L09-L12 look and voice approval
fresh provider quote, balance and enforceable one-job and batch caps
native audio timing and sentence-level edit audit
caption, diagram alt, mobile/desktop and final MP4 review
stop_conditions: source, rights, identity, voice or packet drift
uncertain job outcome or provider error; no retry
cost cap uncertainty or unexpected debit
narration omission, repetition or altered meaning
visual clipping, label collision or unreadable captions
